intro: The Talmud argues. It records questions, proofs, objections and answers, and it often keeps several views side by side. Yet Jewish communities have needed to know what to do on a given day. This unit asks how the rabbis reasoned from a verse to a rule, and how those rules traveled into codes and letters that people still consult.

You will study Rabbi Ishmael's thirteen rules and Rabbi Akiva's close reading, then map how a sugya moves. You will follow the path from the Geonim and Alfasi to Maimonides's Mishneh Torah and Karo's Shulchan Arukh. Then you will read responsa, look at custom, and see how Orthodox, Conservative and Reform Jews reason about electricity, medicine and women's leadership.

By the end, you will be able to trace a ruling from its source to a code, explain why authorities disagree, and describe each movement's view in its own terms. You will also ask, every time, what a ruling protects: the worker, the patient, the stranger, or the life at risk.
bigQuestion: How does Talmudic reasoning turn ancient texts into guidance for new cases, and why do careful readers reach different answers?

timeline.t: Rabbi Ishmael and Rabbi Akiva teach in the Land of Israel
The Mishnah is edited under Rabbi Judah the Prince
The Babylonian Talmud reaches its final form; the age of the Geonim begins
Rav Sherira Gaon writes his letter on how the Mishnah and Talmud were composed
Jacob ben Asher's Arba'ah Turim divides the law into four parts
Joseph Karo's Shulchan Arukh is first printed
The Conservative law committee accepts a responsum permitting electric lights on Shabbat
Reform ordains Sally Priesand, the first woman rabbi in an American seminary
The Chief Rabbinate of Israel accepts brain-stem death under conditions

words.d: the methods for interpreting the Torah that tradition attributes to Rabbi Ishmael
light and heavy; what holds in a lesser case holds all the more in a greater one
verbal analogy between two passages that share a word
one unit of Talmudic discussion on a single topic
a style of analysis from Rabbi Chaim Soloveitchik that defines the concepts under a law
heads of the Babylonian academies, about 600 to 1040 CE
Maimonides's fourteen-book code of Jewish law, completed c. 1180
Joseph Karo's code, first printed in 1565, with Isserles's gloss
a rabbi's written answer to a question of Jewish law
custom; a practice a community keeps, which halakhah often honors
saving a life, which overrides almost every other law
a rabbi who decides questions of Jewish law

test.q: Where is the list of thirteen rules first found?
test.why: The Baraita of Rabbi Ishmael opens the Sifra.

test.q: What does the dayo principle limit?
choices: A light-to-heavy conclusion to the strength of its source
test.why: Dayo says the conclusion cannot exceed its source case.

test.q: Who in Menachot 29b sits in the back of Rabbi Akiva's class?
test.why: The aggadah places Moses in Akiva's study hall.

test.q: What does teiku signal at the end of a sugya?
test.why: Teiku means let it stand, unresolved.

test.q: Which scholar wrote a shortened legal Talmud in the eleventh century?
test.why: Isaac Alfasi (1013–1103) wrote the legal digest.

test.q: Why did some scholars criticize the Mishneh Torah?
choices: It was too short to use
test.why: Critics like the Rabad objected to rulings without their reasons.

test.q: Which code is organized into Orach Chayim, Yoreh De'ah, Even ha-Ezer and Choshen Mishpat?
choices: The Tur and later the Shulchan Arukh
test.why: Jacob ben Asher's Tur set the four parts, and Karo followed them.

test.q: Whose gloss records Ashkenazi practice on the Shulchan Arukh?
What is the main method of reasoning in a responsum?
choices: Comparing a new case to earlier sources and cases
test.why: Responsa reason by comparison to precedent.

test.q: Which Mishnah ties workers' hours to local custom?
test.why: Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:1 follows the custom of the place.

test.q: In Yoma 85b, which verse does Shmuel use to show that life comes first?
test.why: Shmuel cites "he shall live by them."

test.q: Which statement about electricity on Shabbat is accurate?
choices: All movements agree it is forbidden
Authorities compare it to different melakhot and disagree
test.why: Views differ on kindling, building and other comparisons.

test.q: What does Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 teach about one life?
choices: Saving one life is like saving a whole world
One life equals one day of rest
Only a court may save a life
test.why: The Mishnah compares one life to a whole world.

test.q: Which pair disagree in Mishnah Sotah 3:4?
test.why: Ben Azzai and Rabbi Eliezer disagree on teaching daughters Torah.

test.q: In Yoma 83a, whose word decides whether a sick person eats on Yom Kippur?
choices: The patient's, even against a doctor
test.why: The heart knows its own bitterness, so the patient is trusted.

write.prompt: Does Talmudic reasoning mainly aim to protect people? Cite two or three passages from the unit, such as Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:1, Yoma 85b or Yoma 83a, and explain what each says and how different readers have read it.
tips: Name each text you cite, with tractate and page or Mishnah chapter and number.
Attribute every view to its rabbi, code or movement.
Show at least one disagreement and describe both sides fairly.
Use unit terms such as sugya, responsum, minhag and pikuach nefesh.
Compare readings rather than judging which movement is right.
